Josh’s five-minute demo guide

Five AI Tools.
One Unfinished Proposal.

Your team has AI. Why is the work still manual? Follow one client change through five successful AI contributions, then show the coordination Nine-67 can build around them.

The setup

Summit Advisory Group has 150 employees. Leah owns a $750,000 proposal for Northstar Distribution: a 90-day operational improvement engagement at Austin. Five people have completed correct contributions when the client adds Denver.

How to present it

Josh drives the stage and narrates. Keep one dominant object in view and use the primary action to advance each beat. Show one quick AI example, then follow the facts. Leave deep transcripts, architecture and exception controls for Q&A.

0:00 - 0:35 · Scene 1Open scene 1

Everyone finished their part.

Do: Point to the five people, their AI tools and completed contributions. Open one short AI peek, then return to the full team.

“This is Summit Advisory. Leah owns the proposal. Sales has the scope. Delivery has the plan. Finance has the price. Legal has the terms. Marketing has the summary. Every one of these people used AI successfully.”

“Five good outputs. Watch what happens when the client changes one thing.”

Call these five AI workspaces, using ChatGPT, Copilot and Claude. Do not imply five different AI vendors. Everyone’s original output is correct for Austin.

0:35 - 1:00 · Scene 2Open scene 2

Then the client adds Denver.

Do: Reveal Rachel’s email. Point to the three changed requirements: add Denver, retain 90 days, show the additional cost. Advance after Leah acknowledges it.

“Rachel wants Denver included as well as Austin. Same 90-day engagement. Show the extra cost. The proposal is still due Friday.”

“Nobody made a mistake. But now that one change has to travel through five people’s work.”

1:00 - 2:15 · Scene 3Open scene 3

Leah is still connecting everything.

Do: Walk the four manual transfers. Pause on the same facts being carried into the next system. This is the emotional center of the demo.

  1. 1 · Effort“Leah asks Sam what Denver adds. He uses Copilot, reviews the staffing in Jira and replies: 30 additional consultant-days. Parallel staffing keeps the 90-day duration.”
  2. 2 · Pricing“Leah carries that estimate to Priya. Priya uses ChatGPT and the Excel model to review the impact. The fee becomes $810,000. Now Leah has to carry the scope and price together.”
  3. 3 · Terms“She sends the two locations, timing and approved fee to Alex. Alex uses Claude to revise the terms. Leah follows up and tracks which version was reviewed.”
  4. 4 · Assembly“Then she sends the approved pieces to Maya, who uses Copilot to refresh the summary. Leah checks the packet, collects the decisions and gets it ready for final approval.”

“The AI did not fail. Leah is still moving the information and decisions between the tools.”

Do not assign invented minutes or a quantified saving to these actions. Emphasize the visible copying, waiting, version tracking and follow-up. Faster individual revisions do not remove those handoffs.

2:15 - 4:20 · Scene 4Open scene 4

Replay the same change with Nine-67.

Do: Select Run the connected workflow. Let the simulated owner responses play, or use Next owner response to control the pace. Pause for the final approval, which verifies the updates and opens the completed proposal.

  1. Trace“The same email becomes one shared requirement. It links the client scope, delivery plan, price, terms and summary. Each affected owner receives the relevant evidence and the section that needs a decision.”
  2. Owner reviews“These are simulated responses from the named owners. Sam’s approved effort flows to Priya’s review. Her approved price flows into Alex’s terms. Maya receives the approved sections, not five disconnected messages.”
  3. The distinction“Sam still decides whether the staffing works. Priya still owns the price. Alex still owns the terms. What disappears is Leah carrying every answer into the next conversation.”
  4. Final decision“The five owner decisions are recorded against the same revision. Leah can now present one aligned packet for the final leadership decision. Nothing becomes ready simply because the AI drafted it.”
  5. Verify“After the final approval, the workflow updates and checks SharePoint, HubSpot and Jira. If a required update fails, completion stays blocked and the failed step is tracked.”

“We have not added another chatbot to Leah’s day. We have built the workflow that carries the work between the people and systems she already has.”

The owner-response sequence is a demonstration of five recorded decisions, not AI granting approval. The leadership decision remains a separate explicit gate. Six signatures in total must refer to the current revision.

4:20 - 5:00 · Scene 5Open scene 5

One proposal. Ready for the customer.

Do: Show the before-and-after outcome and the final proposal: Austin + Denver, 90 days, $810,000. Point to the approved version and verified destinations. Finish on Leah’s prepared customer reply.

“Before, five people finished their tasks and Leah still had to connect them. Now the requirement, documents and decisions move together into one proposal she can stand behind.”

“We connected their work, their information and their decisions. That is the difference between AI making individual people more productive and AI helping a company finish the work.”

“Bring us one workflow like this. In your complimentary assessment, we’ll map the handoffs, the decisions and where AI can help complete the process.”

Q&A: what Nine-67 would actually build
  1. Connected source records. Permitted access to Outlook, HubSpot, Jira, Excel, Word and SharePoint. Match the opportunity and source versions.
  2. Shared requirements. One versioned record of locations, duration, client commitments and source evidence.
  3. Dependencies and decisions. Route approved effort into pricing, approved pricing into terms, and approved sections into assembly. Track owners, deadlines, reminders and escalation.
  4. Verified completion. Preserve decisions against the correct revision, apply approved updates safely, read back the results and show any partial failure.

The workflow connects approved work products and business records. Do not imply that it automatically reads private AI conversations without configured access.

Q&A: exception walkthroughs
  • A source requirement changes: affected decisions become stale. Re-review the new revision before release.
  • A system update fails: retain the successful steps, keep completion blocked, and retry or route the failed step for recovery.
  • An owner has not approved: the dependent step waits. A reminder or escalation does not replace their decision.

These are optional after the five-minute story. Keep the main walkthrough focused on the visible movement of approved facts.
